draft.title: Geography and the city-states
card: Greece is a rugged land of mountains, with a long, jagged coast and many islands. Travel by land was slow and hard, and the sea linked many places.
Mountains kept communities apart, so each valley or plain grew its own community with its own leaders and laws. These were city-states, called poleis. Athens and Sparta were two of them.
A city-state was a city and the land around it, and it ruled itself. Greeks shared a language and religion, but there was no single Greek country.
Little of the land was good for farming. As populations grew, many Greeks traded by sea for food and goods. Some sailed away to found colonies around the Mediterranean and Black Sea.
draft.remember: Mountains and sea split Greece into separate city-states, and poor farmland pushed Greeks to trade and settle colonies.

a.q: Why did Greece develop many independent city-states rather than one united kingdom?
opts: Mountains and sea kept communities apart
Greeks spoke many unrelated languages
Greek farmland was too rich to share
Persian rulers divided the land into regions
a.why: Mountains made land travel slow, so each community governed itself. Language is wrong because the card says Greeks shared a language, so it did not keep them apart.
a.clue: Think about how the land shaped travel.

b.q: Around 700 BCE, the city-state of Corinth has a growing population but little good farmland. What is a likely response from its people?
opts: Trade by sea and found colonies overseas
Join Athens and Sparta into one country
Stop using ships and farm the mountains
Give up their own laws and leaders
b.why: With poor farmland, Greeks sought food and goods by trade, and some founded colonies abroad. Joining into one country is tempting but wrong, because mountains and sea kept city-states independent.
b.clue: Poor farmland meant they had to look beyond their own land.

wants.brief: A map of ancient Greece showing mountain ranges, the coast, the Aegean islands and the city-states of Athens and Sparta, labelled.
wants.why: It lets students see how mountains and sea separated the city-states.

a.best: Mountains and sea kept communities apart

b.best: Trade by sea and found colonies overseas
